blink.name: Barnard's Star
blink.story: Barnard's Star, the fastest-moving star in the sky: six light-years away. Its centre is burnt out because it is too bright for the camera; NASA flags those pixels.

blink.name: Epsilon Indi B
blink.story: Epsilon Indi B: two brown dwarfs, too small to shine like stars, twelve light-years away.

blink.name: WISE 0855−0714
blink.story: WISE 0855, the coldest brown dwarf known: about −25 °C. It only shows in the reddest light SPHEREx sees, so these plates use detectors 5 and 6 alone.
